evidence.label: Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level

headline: A claimed proof of quantum geometric Langlands duality on any smooth complex curve at every irrational level.
scope: The claim is the unramified de Rham form, for connected simple groups, at shifted levels outside the rational numbers.
plain: Geometric Langlands matches two very different ways of studying bundles of symmetry on a curve. Its quantum form adds a complex number c, the level, and swaps a group G with its Langlands dual. This paper claims the full matching at every level c that is not a fraction. The dual side uses the level −1/(rc), where r is 1, 2 or 3. Rational levels are not covered.
doesNot: This does not cover rational levels, ramified versions, or groups that are not simple.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: A. V. Stoyanovsky, inverse-parameter conjecture attributed to Drinfeld
scorecard.significanceWhy: It claims a central conjecture of the quantum geometric Langlands program in the whole irrational range, including non-real levels.

explanation:
Start with the rule that swaps the levels. Pick a complex number c that is not a fraction, such as c = √2. For the group SL₂ of 2 × 2 matrices with determinant 1, the dual level is −1/c. That is −1/√2, about −0.7071. Some groups have roots of two different lengths. Their lacing number r is 2 or 3; otherwise r = 1[2]. The dual level is then −1/(rc). For r = 2 and c = √2, that gives −1/(2√2), about −0.3536. Doing the swap twice returns c, since −1/(r × (−1/(rc))) = c. Levels need not be real. For r = 1 the level c = i is sent to −1/i = i.

Why exclude fractions? Each level s gives a number q = e^(2πis) on the unit circle. A fraction such as s = 1/3 gives q = e^(2πi/3), and then q³ = 1. So rational levels give roots of unity, and an irrational level never does. The paper's key rank argument works away from roots of unity.

Now the setting. Take X a smooth closed complex curve, such as a sphere or the surface of a doughnut. A G-bundle on X is a family of copies of the group G glued over the curve. All such bundles form one space, Bun_G(X). A D-module on it is, roughly, a system of linear differential equations on that space. The level c twists these equations by a power of a natural line bundle. The Langlands dual group G^∨ comes from G by swapping roots and coroots, the basic directions of its symmetry.

The quantum geometric Langlands conjecture predicts that twisted D-modules for G at level c match those for G^∨ at −1/(rc). Kapustin and Witten's electric–magnetic duality explains the dual group and the reciprocal level[5]. An early form of the conjecture, credited to Drinfeld, appears in Stoyanovsky's 2006 paper[6]. Gaitsgory developed the version in terms of local categories, localization and Whittaker coefficients[7]. Feigin and Frenkel matched W-algebras, algebras of symmetries in two-dimensional field theory, at inverse levels[8]. Campbell, Dhillon and Raskin proved the local equivalences at irrational level[9]. The recent proof of ordinary geometric Langlands supplies the spectral description of the tempered category[10]. Bogdanova built a quantum Langlands functor in the Betti setting, a topological variant[11].

This paper claims the equivalence for every connected simple group, every such curve and every irrational level[1]. It uses the actual global forms and all connected components[3]. It gives the unramified de Rham equivalence in the irrational range[4]. Unramified means no special behaviour is allowed at marked points.

The route goes through localization. Localization turns representations of loop algebras into twisted D-modules on the space of bundles[12]. The paper first compares the two sides on such localized objects. Two global Whittaker identities then give the inverses of the resulting functor[13]. One obstacle is a deformation step for a global kernel. The paper controls it with a new weight argument[14]. Ranks of certain maps stay constant away from roots of unity. That gives the needed vanishing at every irrational level[15].

How sure is this? There is no Lean scope note for this result, so no computer proof checker has tested it. The paper relies on the long recent proof of ordinary geometric Langlands and on many other inputs. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if the proof holds. It is one long paper resting on large recent works, with no Lean scope note. No specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: A family of copies of a symmetry group G glued together over a curve.
Roughly, a system of linear differential equations on a space.
A complex number that twists the D-modules on the space of bundles.
The group obtained from G by swapping its roots and coroots.
1, 2 or 3, the ratio of squared lengths of the long and short roots of the group.
A complex number q with qⁿ = 1 for some whole number n ≥ 1.
A way of turning representations of loop algebras into D-modules on the space of bundles.
